title: Student who filmed in women's toilets is put on sex offender register
text:
By ASHLEY NICKEL, NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA and SARAH BROOKES - SENIOR REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  23:59 AEST, 8 September 2026   |  Updated:  00:10 AEST, 9 September 2026

The courts have reversed a highly criticised decision to allow a student to walk away without conviction after filming dozens of women inside public toilets and showers.

Vietnamese student Bao Phuc Cao, 24, returned to Melbourne Magistrates' Court on Monday and had his name added to the sex offender registry.

Cao, a biomedicine student at the University of Melbourne, pleaded guilty to secretly filming a woman inside a Docklands shopping centre bathroom in February 2025.

Police later uncovered more than 100 similar videos on his devices but were unable to determine the exact number of victims.

The serial upskirter was handed a community corrections order and two good behaviour bonds in March, without a mark on his criminal record.

The case exploded internationally after Tesla billionaire Elon Musk weighed in on X, responding to a post from activist Drew Pavlou, who wrote: 'He filmed 150 Australian women in toilets. Zero conviction. Judge didn't want to deport him.'

Musk replied: 'Deport the judge.'

On Monday, Cao's defence argued he shouldn't be placed on the sex offender registry because it was a 'lifelong consequence' and he hadn't committed further offences.

Bao Phuc Cao (above) had his name added to the sex offenders registry on Monday

Cao (above) was found to have over 100 videos of women using public bathrooms

However, Magistrate Michelle Mykytowycz ruled Cao posed a risk to the 'sexual safety' of women in Melbourne.

Cao will be monitored by police for the next eight years and subject to strict reporting conditions.

He's also banned from working with children and it will be difficult, if not impossible, for him to work in high-risk industries, including medicine.

A person is not able to become a registered health practitioner in Australia if their criminal history is 'inconsistent with suitability to hold registration or practise the profession'.

In an interview shown to the court, Cao admitted: 'Sometimes it just makes me feel excited to film the girls.'

The court previously heard that Cao's behaviour had a 'profound impact' on one victim, who now struggles to use public bathrooms at work or in public.

She 'panicked' after she noticed Cao's phone pointed at her from under a cubicle wall at Chipmunks Playland and Cafe Docklands on February 20, 2025.

Security was informed and swooped on Cao, who was in a nearby toilet cubicle.

Cao (centre) will be subject to strict police monitoring for the next eight years

The March sentencing was the third time Cao avoided jail time for the same type of predatory behaviour.

In October 2024, he was caught filming a woman in a public bathroom and ultimately received a community corrections order.

In July 2025, Cao again received lenient treatment without a recorded conviction for an offence in student showers.
